title: bin/cairn.py lays the instance wiring the bash launcher laid, so cairn.cmd loses none of it
intention: bin/cairn.py carries bootstrap.sh's cairn_wire_instances: before it dispatches, an instance root missing a device's instance bin has the class bin's verbs linked (or copied where Windows cannot link) into it.
why: Measured: 2026-11-20 on akiendell (Windows), at main d4b139be4: with CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT pointing at an empty temp directory, 'bash bin/cairn probescan' leaves 58 entries under it (bin/cairn _floor_instance sources bootstrap.sh and runs cairn_wire_instances), and 'bin\cairn.cmd probescan' leaves 0. cairn.cmd now runs bin/cairn.py, which ports the dispatch but not the floor's wiring, so a fresh Windows instance root is no longer wired by typing cairn. Landed by ticket 380d524e6e9c.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured); Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine: a crossing's record is committed where it lands); Law 9 (green is earned).
how: A hypothesis, not a settled shape: bin/cairn.py runs a small _wire_instances before dispatch, a Python port of cairn_wire_instances' per-file rule (link when absent, repoint a stale link, leave a hand-placed file and say so), skipped for help. Depends on 380d524e6e9c; 8b94ca4536c9 (the Linux exec) must carry the same clause so Linux does not drop the wiring.

clauses.claim: with an empty CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT, bin\cairn.cmd probescan leaves the same set of instance bin entries bash bin/cairn probescan leaves
a hand-placed file where a class verb would link is left in place and named on stderr
cairn.cmd help wires nothing, as the bash launcher's help wires nothing
